Container.Name: hikari-index
Container.Overview:
A local-first reference library of anime stills. Pick an episode or a film and Hikari Index pulls a small set of representative frames from it, with palette, composition, tags and similarity search, and serves them from a gallery on your own network. Your video is read-only and never leaves the machine.
This is the all-in-one container: the gallery, its database, the worker that reads your video and the text encoder for mood search. It makes its own passwords on the first start; the admin password is printed in this container's log, which is the only place it is kept, so write it down then.
It does not describe the frames or pick the stills. That is the analyze worker: install "hikari-index-analyze" as well (CPU, on this server), or run a GPU worker on another machine (see the docs). Until one is running, added work waits after its first step.
Container.ExtraSearchTerms: anime stills screenshots frames cinematography gallery
Container.Requires: The first start prints the admin password in the log (Docker tab, the container's icon, Logs); the log goes when the container is updated, so write it down. Then install hikari-index-analyze, or connect an analyze worker on another machine.

Config.Name: Web port
Config.Description: The port the gallery is opened on.

Config.Name: Gallery address
Config.Description: The address you will open the gallery at, exactly as in the browser's address bar, for example http://192.168.1.10:5183 or http://tower.local:5183. The admin sign-in refuses a form sent from any other address.

Config.Name: Video
Config.Description: The folder your video is in. Read-only: nothing here is ever changed.

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: Where the original frames and run records are kept. The largest folder: about 1 GB an episode until you finish reviewing it, about 150 MB after. A share on the array is fine.

Config.Name: Web images
Config.Description: The images the gallery shows, about 15 MB an episode. They are read on every page view, so keep them on a pool that does not spin down. They can be made again from Data.

Config.Name: Config
Config.Description: The database, the passwords the container makes, and a daily database dump (backups/, fourteen kept). Back this folder up.

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: The user the programs run as and that owns the files they write. If you change PUID or PGID, change --user in hikari-index-analyze's Extra Parameters to the same pair, or it cannot read its token.

Config.Name: Shoko address
Config.Description: Optional. Your Shoko server, for example http://192.168.1.10:8111, to pick episodes from its catalog (read-only). Put a non-admin API key, alone, in a file named shoko-api-key in the Config folder. With Shoko, also set Source folders.

Config.Name: Source folders
Config.Description: A name for the Video folder. With Shoko the name is Shoko's managed folder id, for example 4=/source.

Config.Name: Working hours
Config.Description: Optional. Only start reading video and making images between these hours, for example 01-07, on the server's clock. Empty runs whenever there is work.

Config.Name: Time zone
Config.Description: Optional. The time zone Working hours and the times in the log are in, for example America/New_York. Empty is this server's own time zone.

Config.Name: Check for work every
Config.Description: How often the worker that reads your video asks for work when it has none, in seconds. The analyze container has its own field for this.

Config.Name: More analyze workers
Config.Description: Optional. Tokens for analyze workers on other machines, as name:token,name:token. The analyze container on this server needs nothing here.

Config.Name: Footer notice
Config.Description: Optional. A line of your own text at the foot of every page, for example credits for openly licensed video. Web addresses in it become links.

Config.Name: Admin link
Config.Description: 0 hides the Admin link in the page header. The link only: /admin still answers.

Config.Name: Admin name
Config.Description: Optional. The admin sign-in name. Empty is admin.
